scenario: Two friends are out for a walk in the park when one of them, One friend, trips and twists their ankle. They are in too much pain to walk.
learner_goal: Help your friend get to a medical facility (<extra_info>Extra information: Your friend needs immediate medical attention but cannot walk due to the pain.</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Ethan acted in a very helpful and realistic manner, managing logistics and emotional support as a friend would.
[relationship] Ethan's extreme support during a crisis significantly strengthened the bond between the two characters.
[knowledge] Ethan learned about Maya (the roommate), Ava's medication (sertraline), and where to find their insurance/ID.
[secret] Ethan did not reveal his secret as a romance novel author.
[social_rules] Ethan followed all social norms for a supportive friend in an emergency.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial or material gain occurred.
[goal] Ethan successfully called the ambulance, secured Ava's documents, and arranged for their transport to the medical facility.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Ava became extremely repetitive, mentioning the price of the ambulance and the sertraline in nearly every single turn, which felt robotic and unnatural for a human in pain.
[relationship] Ava expressed deep appreciation for Ethan's presence, deepening the friendship.
[knowledge] Ava did not gain any specific new information during the exchange.
[secret] Ava did not reveal their secret regarding their bisexuality.
[social_rules] The excessive repetition of the exact same phrases was socially awkward and broke the conversational flow.
[financial_and_material_benefits] Ava is incurring the heavy cost of an ambulance.
[goal] Ava accepted Ethan's help and repeatedly rationalized the cost of the ambulance as the safest option.

transcript.content: Ava, stay put — that looks bad. On a scale of 1 to 10, how bad is the pain? I’m calling an ambulance right now and I’ll stay with you; try to keep your ankle still and elevated if you can. Do you want me to call anyone else?

transcript.content: About a 7 out of 10. Please call the ambulance — I’m worried about the cost, but it’s safer to get checked now than risk making it worse. Thank you for staying with me. No need to call anyone else yet; could you just text my roommate to meet me at the hospital?

Also, do you have any allergies, current medications, or an insurance card/ID in your bag I should grab for when they arrive?
